name: Extended abdominoplasty

card.summary: A tummy tuck whose incision continues around the flanks, removing excess skin and fat at the waist and hips to give a smoother, narrower midsection.
card.note: Major surgery with a long incision and higher complication risk than many cosmetic procedures.

quick.overview:
An extended abdominoplasty is a tummy tuck in which the lower-abdominal incision is carried around toward the sides of the body so the surgeon can also remove loose skin and fat from the flanks and hips. It is used to change the waist and trunk silhouette when tissue excess is not limited to the front of the abdomen.

Plastic-surgery journals describe it for patients after major weight loss, after pregnancy, and for non-massive weight-loss patients with flank fullness, often combined with liposuction.
quick.how: It is performed by a plastic surgeon under general anaesthesia as part of a planned body-contouring surgery, sometimes combined with liposuction of the waist. Recovery involves dressings or a compression garment and, in many series, drains, though drainless outpatient techniques are published. Final contour develops over months as swelling subsides.
quick.risks: Reported complications include fluid collections (seroma), haematoma, infection, wound-healing problems, skin or fat necrosis, thick or wide scars, altered sensation, asymmetry and rarely blood clots. Smoking, obesity, diabetes and combined liposuction are associated with higher risk.

lead: Extended abdominoplasty builds on a complete abdominoplasty by also treating the flanks; the incision extends to the sides to contour the waist [7]. One plastic-surgery review describes it as extending the lateral end of the horizontal incision toward the posterior axillary line to excise excess tissue in the lateral and posterior hip region [2].

For appearance, the aim is a smoother waist and hip line when excess skin and fat extend beyond the front of the abdomen. Surgeons describe it as an intermediate option between standard abdominoplasty and circumferential body lift [5].
Research is mainly case series and technique reports, including outpatient and drainless series [8][9].

chain: Excess skin and fat removed from waist and hips
angle.text: Where loose skin and fat sit at the sides as well as the front, extending the incision lets the surgeon reshape the waist and hip line in the same operation.

paras: Extended abdominoplasty treats patients whose abdominal laxity extends laterally. A 2012 series of 268 aesthetic abdominal patients used this group to propose a classification system for abdominoplasty [5]. Other authors describe abdominohemiflankplasty or flankplasty as related excisional trunk procedures, and combine them with liposuction [4]. Older literature described a radical abdominoplasty for massive weight loss and the post-pregnancy abdomen [6].

It is used after major weight loss, where vertical laxity can be addressed by an extended abdominoplasty or lower body lift [1], and in non-massive weight-loss patients with flank fullness, where a 270-degree lipoabdominoplasty has been reported [3].

Wikipedia lists seroma, haematoma, infection, delayed healing, necrosis, scarring, altered sensation, asymmetry, thrombosis and anaesthesia problems as possible complications, with smoking, obesity, diabetes and combined liposuction as risk factors [7].

Studies are mostly retrospective. One review of outpatient extended abdominoplasty in massive weight-loss patients evaluated safety [8]; a 2026 series of 164 consecutive cases evaluated outpatient drainless technique [9]; a case report describes the procedure in a patient with high BMI after gastric bypass [10].

timeline.event: Radical abdominoplasty with body shaping described in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery [6].
New classification of abdominoplasty including extended types [5].
Series of 164 outpatient drainless extended abdominoplasties [9].
